goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — P1 confidence 100: when callers omit `externalCalendarId`, the fallback compares every ID to `undefined` instead of selecting the event destination, so Google update receives an undefined calendarId rather than the selected calendar.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 253-256 in the diff: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is undefined/falsy, the fallback uses `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` which compares each calendar's externalId to undefined. This will never match any calendar (unless a calendar has externalId === undefined), so the find will return undefined, and selectedCalendar will be undefined. This is clearly a bug - the fallback logic is broken. The same pattern appears at line 314-316 for deleteEvent. This is a real logic error introduced in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at line 117-119 in EventManager.ts: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is undefined or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`. Accessing `.integration` on `undefined` will throw a TypeError. This is a real bug - the code should check if `mainHostDestinationCalendar` exists before accessing its properties, like `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or add a null check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-261 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId; ... calendarId: selectedCalendar` — P1 confidence 100: when a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, the fallback searches for `externalId === undefined` instead of selecting its destination calendar, producing an undefined calendarId and making Google updates fail for that valid legacy/reference shape.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the updateEvent method in GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code at lines 253-255 shows: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When externalCalendarId is falsy (undefined/null), the fallback logic searches for a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `cal.externalId === undefined`), which will never match any valid calendar entry. This means the fallback will always return undefined, causing the calendar update to potentially fail or use wrong defaults. This is a clear logical bug - the fallback should likely use a different approach like selecting the first destination calendar or matching by credentialId, similar to how createEvent handles it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-370 — `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar) { ... const credentialFromDB = await prisma.credential.findUnique(...) ... const createdEvent = await createEvent(...) }` — P2 confidence 100: collective bookings perform a serial credential query and serial provider call per destination calendar, creating an N+1/linear latency cliff as team size grows.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code in createAllCalendarEvents iterates through destination calendars sequentially with `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and performs database queries (`prisma.credential.findUnique`) and API calls (`createEvent`) inside the loop. This is indeed a serial/sequential pattern that could cause latency issues as the number of destination calendars grows. However, this is more of a performance optimization concern rather than a bug or correctness issue. The code will function correctly, just potentially slower with many calendars. Additionally, the credential lookup from DB is only a fallback when the credential isn't found in the local cache, so the N+1 pattern only occurs in edge cases. This is a valid performance concern but not a critical bug.
